notes: Identity verified from title block: On the Association Between Loneliness and Bathing Habits: Nine Replications of Bargh and Shalev (2012) Study 1; M. Brent Donnellan, Richard E. Lucas, and Joseph Cesario; Emotion 2015, 15(1),109–119; DOI 10.1037/a0036079. Full primary commentary/report text with Methods, Results, tables, and references, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied; layout not independently rendered. Original statistics are unassigned placeholders, not unavailable-source findings. Screened mTurk sample: Bargh-Shalev loneliness with index r=.08,p=.058,n=553; UCLA loneliness with index r=.03,p=.488,n=553. Temperature correlations: Table 2 prints r=.09 for Bargh-Shalev and r=.05 for UCLA (footnote), with respective p=.047 and .252 in text; Table 2 gives study N range 551–553 without test-specific temperature N. All relevant-data index: Bargh-Shalev r=.08,p=.057,n=569; UCLA r=.03,p=.508,n=566. Table 3 instead uses average z-scored loneliness scales, yielding index r=.06 and temperature r=.07, not either individual scale. Honesty Yes and correct rarely response; approximately 97% retained. Index N=553 common to both screened loneliness scales; temperature-specific N unresolved within printed range 551–553. No candidates promoted to target statistics because the locator identifies a study/page but not a unique outcome/test. Printed r metrics retained without conversion. Reported-success entries describe the authors’ study-level narrative; they do not resolve statistic correspondence.
